description: Warehouse CITY is an open-source dashboard by Radical Research (Mike McCarthy), described with Susan A. Phillips in a 2024 Environment and Planning B article, that maps warehouses and estimates their cumulative impacts in Southern California. Contents: warehouse parcels identified from county assessor databases, shown as polygons on an interactive map, with summary and per-warehouse tables of count, acreage, building footprint, estimated heavy-duty truck trips, diesel particulate matter, NOx and CO2 emissions, and jobs, for existing and planned or approved warehouses in any user-drawn area; advanced users can change inputs such as average truck trip length (38 miles by default). Coverage: Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside and San Bernardino counties, just under 20 million people; the Inland Empire alone has about 4,000 warehouses. Format and access: a free Shiny web app. Licence and cost: presented as open source and public; no licence named on the pages read. Caveats: emissions use basin-wide averages, and the tool was built to support community groups, so it is informational. The parcel list and truck and emission estimates link freight land use to air pollution and environmental justice exposure for hazard exposure and network flow studies of goods movement. It relates to the Freight Analysis Framework in the catalogue.
